title: Reality and Complexity of $F$-symbols in $2+1$d Topological Phases
authors: Matthew Buican, Peter Huston, Jiannis K. Pachos
abstract: The $F$-symbols of an anyon theory encode the associativity of fusion and constitute some of the theory's most fundamental and, simultaneously, subtle data. Much of the subtlety lies in the gauge-dependence of the $F$-symbols. Despite their generic complexity, many braided anyon theories admit gauges in which all $F$-symbols are real, a phenomenon for which no general organising principle has been known. We identify a physical mechanism underlying this reality. For a unitary ribbon fusion category admitting an appropriate braided charge-conjugation symmetry, we show that the complex-conjugated $F$-symbols are related to the original ones by a gauge transformation. Finding a real gauge is thereby reduced to a condition on these transformations. When the charge-conjugation symmetry is suitably "flat,'' or equivalently when the associated "twisted'' Frobenius-Schur (or "generalized'' Kawanaka-Matsuyama) data respects a grading, these local transformations can be trivialised and a real gauge exists. This framework unifies a broad range of previously disparate examples, including families of Chern-Simons theories whose $F$-symbols are difficult to directly compute. Finally, we exhibit a unitary ribbon category that realizes a novel obstruction to the existence of a real gauge and therefore has inherently complex $F$-symbols.
summary: This work establishes a deep physical principle governing when the fundamental F-symbols of anyon theories can be made real in a gauge. By linking this reality condition to the flatness of the charge-conjugation symmetry, the authors provide a unifying framework for understanding topological phases. This is significant because it offers a concrete, symmetry-based criterion for classifying quantum materials exhibiting topological order.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the physical conditions under which the F-symbols, which encode the associativity of fusion in anyon theories, can be made real via a suitable gauge transformation.
main_result: The reality of the F-symbols is shown to be governed by a physical mechanism related to the flatness of the braided charge-conjugation symmetry within the associated unitary ribbon category.
method: The authors analyze the relationship between the F-symbols and their complex conjugates using gauge transformations, reducing the problem to a condition on the symmetry structure of the category.
model_or_system: The theory is formulated using Unitary Modular Tensor Categories (UMTCs) that model $2+1$ dimensional Topological Quantum Field Theories (TQFTs) and anyon models, including families of Chern-Simons theories.
key_observables: The F-symbols, which quantify the associativity of fusion, and the associated R-matrices.
important_parameters: The structure of the charge-conjugation symmetry, specifically its 'flatness' or the grading property of the associated Frobenius-Schur data.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a unitary ribbon category and relies on relating the reality condition to the trivialization of local gauge transformations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the concept of 'flatness' in the context of the charge-conjugation symmetry, showing the required triviality of the holonomy at fusion vertices.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first establishing the gauge equivalence between F-symbols and their conjugates, then linking this equivalence to the physical condition of charge-conjugation symmetry, and finally showing that 'flatness' of this symmetry guarantees the existence of a real gauge.
why_interesting: The connection between topological invariants (F-symbols) and symmetry constraints (charge-conjugation flatness) provides a powerful, general principle for classifying realizable quantum phases, which is relevant for understanding emergent symmetries in strongly correlated electron systems.
